macroNarrative: Indian equities are caught between a constructive domestic story and a noisy external one. Inflation at multi-year lows, a rate-cutting cycle largely complete, healthy corporate balance sheets, and rural demand finally turning all support a long view. The crosswinds — INR at record lows around 94–95/USD, Brent above $100 on West Asia tension, an FII flow picture that has been net-negative for many months, and small/mid-cap valuations roughly 40% above their 10-year average — argue for selectivity, not absence.

conviction.name: HDFC Bank
conviction.thesis: India's largest private-sector bank, finally past its post-merger digestion. Asset quality is at a multi-year best, the governance review is clearing, and the franchise's deposit-gathering machine is unmatched. The valuation has stopped being demanding.
catalysts: Governance review clearing path for CEO reappointment
NIM stabilisation post HDFC Ltd merger absorption
Retail credit cycle turning supportive in FY27
risks: Net interest margin pressure if RBI eases further
Heavy index weight invites foreign-flow volatility

conviction.name: ICICI Bank
conviction.thesis: The best-run large bank in India by almost any operating metric — consistent ROA above 2%, conservative provisioning, a digital stack peers are still trying to replicate. We pay a premium happily.
catalysts: Cleaner book than every private peer
Fee income compounding at double digits
risks: Valuation premium leaves less room for error

conviction.name: State Bank of India
conviction.thesis: The flagship PSU. Asset quality is at its cleanest in a decade, ROE has migrated above 16%, and it trades at roughly 1.5× book — versus 2.5–3× for private peers with similar returns. Government backing is a feature, not a bug, for the patient.
catalysts: Subsidiary value (SBI Cards, SBI Life, AMC) under-counted in price
Beneficiary of credit growth + lower bond yields
risks: Government cross-currents (PSL targets, minority stake sales)
Treasury volatility in rate cycle turns
Slower fee-income growth than private peers

conviction.name: ITC
conviction.thesis: A cash-printing cigarette monopoly funding a steadily compounding FMCG business, plus hotels, paperboards, and agri. Near-zero debt, a 3.5%+ dividend yield, and a hotels demerger that should unlock value the consolidated structure has long obscured.
catalysts: FMCG margins continuing to expand toward HUL's
risks: FMCG rural demand recovery has been uneven
Tobacco-related ESG screens limit some institutional buying

conviction.name: Bharat Electronics
conviction.thesis: The crown jewel of Indian defence indigenisation. Order book over ₹75,000 Cr giving multi-year revenue visibility, ROCE above 25%, debt-free balance sheet, and a customer (Government of India) that is structurally increasing capex on home-built systems.
catalysts: Defence capex growing at low-double digits in FY27 budget
Export orders compounding from a small base
risks: Valuation multiple is the highest in its history

conviction.name: Power Finance Corp
conviction.thesis: Government-backed NBFC at the centre of India's power and renewables financing build-out. Trades at a single-digit P/E with a ~4% dividend yield, ROE in the high teens, and a loan book with vastly improved asset quality after the Discom clean-up.
catalysts: Renewable energy financing the dominant growth driver
Re-rating potential as discom risk is repriced
risks: Concentration in power sector / discom credit risk
Bond market volatility on long-dated lending book

conviction.name: Oil & Natural Gas Corp
conviction.thesis: The classic deep-value PSU: P/E around 7–8×, P/B near 1×, dividend yield over 4%, and a direct beneficiary of crude staying elevated on West Asia tensions. The market continues to price in disasters that have not happened.
catalysts: Gas price reform supporting earnings floor
risks: Sharp crude correction if geopolitical risk eases
Capex cycle pressure on free cash flow

conviction.name: Coforge
conviction.thesis: The bright spot in a battered IT sector. Q4 net profit grew 145% YoY, deal wins are accelerating, and the AI / cloud positioning is pulling clients from the giants. One of the few IT names where the 12-month set-up looks better than the 12-month rear-view.
catalysts: Deal wins outpacing Tier-1 IT in the same quarter
AI services book gaining real revenue traction
risks: IT sector sentiment remains poor — multiple compression risk
Higher beta than large-cap IT in any global slowdown

conviction.name: Bajaj Auto
conviction.thesis: April sales were a blockbuster — exports up 83% YoY, CV growth strong, EV ramp underway. A two-wheeler franchise with global reach, a clean balance sheet, healthy buybacks, and a serious EV bet through Chetak.
catalysts: Export tailwind back after a multi-year drought
risks: EV margin profile still being established

conviction.name: Reliance Industries
conviction.thesis: The default India mega-cap, with three engines now visible: Jio (telecom + monetisation), Reliance Retail (largest retailer in the country), and a maturing oil-to-chemicals business funding a serious new-energy platform. Multiple value-unlock paths over a decade.
catalysts: Jio tariff hike cycle still has runway
Reliance Retail IPO talk persists as latent catalyst
New energy capex starting to produce revenue
risks: Conglomerate discount may persist longer than expected

highPromise.name: Computer Age Management Services
highPromise.thesis: A duopoly providing the picks-and-shovels for India's mutual fund industry. Q4 EBITDA margin expanded to 46.3%, profit grew 11%. As MF AUM compounds at 15%+ annually, CAMS rides that wave with operating leverage.
catalysts: MF industry AUM growth structural at 15%+
New product wins (alt fund servicing, AIFs)

highPromise.name: Wockhardt
highPromise.thesis: Posted a turnaround Q4 — ₹164 Cr profit versus a ₹45 Cr loss a year ago. The novel antibiotic pipeline (Zaynich, others) is reaching commercial inflection. Speculative but asymmetric.

highPromise.name: Himachal Futuristic
highPromise.thesis: Optical fibre cable, 5G transmission gear, and a small but growing defence electronics order book. India's 5G + BharatNet + defence comms theme captured in one mid-cap name.
catalysts: Defence segment scaling from a small base
risks: Margin pressure from raw material moves

highPromise.name: Suzlon Energy
highPromise.thesis: A fully restructured balance sheet, the largest order book in its history, and a wind capacity addition cycle just starting after years of dormancy. High beta — sized accordingly, not avoided.
catalysts: Net-debt-free for the first time in a decade

highPromise.name: IdeaForge Technology
highPromise.thesis: Recently jumped ~30% on a 7× YoY revenue surge and a return to profit. Pure-play on Indian military and homeland-security drone procurement, an area where indigenisation policy is accelerating. Lottery-ticket sized, not core.

watchClose.name: Tata Consultancy Services
watchClose.thesis: The bluest of blue chips, but caught in a sector-wide air pocket. Quality of business is unchanged; what has changed is the cyclical demand picture from US BFSI clients. We hold; we do not chase.
catalysts: AI services adoption with marquee clients
risks: Wage inflation if attrition climbs again

watchClose.name: Infosys
watchClose.thesis: Same story as TCS, slightly cheaper. Operating margins are pinched, but the franchise, balance sheet and capital return habit are intact. Not a sell, just not yet a buy.
catalysts: Margin recovery as discretionary spend returns

watchClose.name: Hindustan Unilever
watchClose.thesis: Volume growth has finally returned (~6% recently) and the FY27 outlook is brighter — but at ~55× earnings, you are paying for a perfect recovery. Trim, don't add. A correction is the friend, not the enemy.
catalysts: Margin recovery once palm oil cools
risks: Valuation leaves no room for misses

watchClose.name: Asian Paints
watchClose.thesis: The franchise is real, the brand is real — but Birla Opus from the Aditya Birla group is the most credible threat to the moat in twenty years. Until we see how share-loss settles, holding is the right answer; adding is not.
risks: Multiple still rich for the new growth profile

watchClose.name: Larsen & Toubro
watchClose.thesis: Just guided FY27 revenue growth lower on Middle East disruptions. The long-cycle infra story is unchanged, but the next 2–3 quarters look choppier than the consensus had assumed. Hold; let the dust settle.
catalysts: Domestic infra & defence order pipeline intact
Middle East order book recovery once tensions ease
risks: West Asia exposure to conflict risk
Margin guidance has been reset down
Capex slowdown if elections shift policy

watchClose.name: Bharti Airtel
watchClose.thesis: Best-positioned in a duopoly, with strong ARPU momentum and Africa optionality. But the stock has already priced much of the next two years of tariff hikes. We hold what we have; we don't add aggressively here.
risks: Premium valuation vs. global telecom peers

trimAvoid.name: Trent
trimAvoid.thesis: Zudio is a brilliant business; Trent at this price is a brilliant business priced as if it cannot stumble. Single-month drawdowns of 22% in such names are reminders that valuation matters. Trim into strength.
risks: P/E above 100× is structurally hard to defend
Any same-store-sales miss is asymmetrically punished

trimAvoid.name: Avenue Supermarts
trimAvoid.thesis: A great business with a slowing growth equation. Quick-commerce is reshaping the urban grocery basket faster than DMart's store-led model can respond. The valuation still assumes the old growth trajectory; the new one is materially lower.

trimAvoid.name: Nestle India
trimAvoid.thesis: An exceptional brand portfolio at a price that demands exceptional growth — which has not been delivered. Volume growth has been mid-single-digit; the multiple is double that of global staples. Hold a small position at most.
risks: Valuation vs. growth gap is the largest in years

trimAvoid.name: Eternal (Zomato)
trimAvoid.thesis: Blinkit is genuinely interesting; the valuation prices in it being interesting forever. With Swiggy and Reliance escalating quick-commerce capex, the path to durable profitability is narrower than the share price suggests.
risks: Quick-commerce profitability still unproven at scale

longBets.name: Syrma SGS Technology
longBets.thesis: Top brokerage pick in Indian Electronics Manufacturing Services. The sector grew 24% CAGR FY19-24 and is forecast at 27% to FY29 on the back of PLI schemes, China+1 supply-chain shifts, and rising domestic electronics demand. Margin expansion is structural as backward integration deepens. India's EMS market share is under 5% globally — it is heading higher.
catalysts: FY26-28E revenue CAGR estimated at 29%, profit CAGR 44% by HDFC Sec
PLI scheme extension expected; budget tailwinds
Aerospace/defence/healthcare mix shift improving margins by 130bps
risks: Single-quarter margin volatility on input costs

longBets.name: Praj Industries
longBets.thesis: India's largest biofuel technology company — ethanol, bio-CNG, sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), water treatment. The stock is down ~30% over 12 months on a temporary order pause and a Q3 loss; but the structural opportunity in ethanol blending (E20 mandate), 2G ethanol, and SAF is intact. A textbook 'Mr. Market' moment.
catalysts: Order book recovering after temporary pause
Stock at 52-week low region offers valuation comfort
risks: Recent quarterly loss reflects execution slippage
Crude price collapse would dampen biofuel economics

longBets.name: Data Patterns (India)
longBets.thesis: The pure-play on Indian indigenous radar, electronic warfare, and avionics — supplying BEL, HAL, ISRO, DRDO. FY25 revenue grew 36% YoY, EBITDA margins around 39% (rare for defence). Order momentum strong. The franchise quality is exceptional; the entry price will always feel uncomfortable.
catalysts: FY27 budget targeting 'Force Multipliers' (electronic warfare, drone swarms)
Confirmed orders ~₹900 Cr with more in the pipeline
Tejas Mk1A and indigenous platform build-out
risks: Valuation at 60×+ leaves zero margin for error

longBets.name: MTAR Technologies
longBets.thesis: High-precision component supplier to defence, aerospace, civilian nuclear, and clean energy (fuel cells, electrolysers). Niche, hard-to-replicate manufacturing capabilities. Recently won a $3.78m order in data-centre infrastructure, opening a new vertical.
catalysts: Clean energy fuel-cell components scaling globally
Order book healthy across multiple verticals
risks: Valuation at 165× P/E is the most stretched among peers
Single new-vertical bets carry execution risk

longBets.name: Astra Microwave Products
longBets.thesis: RF and microwave subsystems for radars, electronic warfare, and satellite payloads. Q3 FY26 profit jumped 96% QoQ; operating margins expanded to 31.7%. Trades cheaper than peers (P/E 53 vs DataPatterns 62, MTAR 165). Government's indigenous AESA radar push is a multi-year tailwind.
catalysts: 12.4% rise in DRDO R&D funding for indigenous AESA radars
Q3 margins jumped to 31.7% on better mix
5-year stock return 660%+ vs Sensex 62%, but pulled back recently — entry window
risks: ROE at 10.5% lags Garden Reach (20%) and Data Patterns (13%)
Beta of 1.35 means sharper drawdowns in selloffs

longBets.name: KNR Constructions
longBets.thesis: Roads and highways EPC contractor with one of the cleanest balance sheets in the construction space — rare for the sector. Government's NHAI awards remain a reliable pipeline, and KNR has consistently delivered above-industry execution.
catalysts: Margin profile better than larger peers
risks: Asset monetisation pace slower than hoped
Construction cycle exposure to monsoon delays

longBets.name: Maharashtra Seamless
longBets.thesis: India's largest seamless pipe manufacturer for oil & gas, power, and infrastructure. Debt-free, 19.6% operating margins, 3-year profit CAGR ~69%. A cyclical play with structural tailwinds from domestic oil & gas capex and energy transition.
catalysts: Debt-free balance sheet allows organic capex
risks: Concentration in oil & gas customer base

longBets.name: Ion Exchange (India)
longBets.thesis: Pioneer in water and wastewater treatment in India. ROCE of 27.5%, debt-equity 0.2, operating across municipal, industrial, and household water. Direct beneficiary of Jal Jeevan Mission and increasingly stringent industrial effluent norms.
catalysts: Jal Jeevan Mission and similar government water programs
Premium consumer water purifier brand (Zero B)
risks: Working capital intensity in EPC contracts
Smaller order sizes vs MNC competitors

sectors.name: Private Banking
sectors.note: Asset quality at a decadal best; rate-cut cycle is essentially done. Reasonable valuations on the leaders.

sectors.name: PSU Banking
sectors.note: Cleanest books in years, single-digit P/Es on the largest names. The discount to private peers is closing.

sectors.name: Information Technology
sectors.note: Global headwinds linger; large-caps look full. We are selective on mid-cap names with AI traction.

sectors.name: FMCG
sectors.note: Recovery underway but priced into most names. Demand defensiveness has been rewarded — perhaps too much.

sectors.name: Auto
sectors.note: Two-wheelers re-accelerating, exports rebounding, EV transition creating winners and losers in equal measure.

sectors.name: Pharma
sectors.note: US generics cycle stable, domestic chronic therapy compounding. A quietly good place to be.

sectors.name: Real Estate
sectors.note: Rate cuts behind us are still flowing through; inventory cycle remains supportive in top-7 cities.

sectors.name: Capital Goods / Infra
sectors.note: Order books healthy, but execution and margins under pressure — wait for better entry on the leaders.

sectors.name: Energy / Oil & Gas
sectors.note: Upstream benefits from elevated crude; OMCs will lag if marketing margins remain regulated.

sectors.name: Defence
sectors.note: Multi-year visibility on indigenisation orders. The valuation is the only question, not the demand.

sectors.name: Renewables
sectors.note: Capacity addition pipeline finally translating into revenue. Selectivity matters — execution track records are mixed.

sectors.name: Quick-Commerce / Internet
sectors.note: Reflexive valuations; the capex war is intensifying, not resolving. Path to profit is narrowing, not widening.

earnings.name: Urban Company
earnings.watch: First post-IPO read on contribution margins

whispers.text: IPO pipeline rebuilds after a record 2025 — eyes on consumer-tech and renewables filings.
FY27 defence capex expected at the high end of the 13–15% range; BEL, HAL and shipyards are the obvious vehicles.
US–Iran negotiation chatter drives oil-sensitive sectors both ways. Upstream is the cleanest hedge.
INR at record lows around 94–95/USD pressures import-heavy sectors; favours IT & pharma exporters at the margin.
Rural recovery genuinely improving on a strong-monsoon read; FMCG volumes the cleanest signal to track.
Private capex announcements broadening — cement, metals, autos. Capital-goods order pipeline still building.
